requirements.requirement: Discover which physical interfaces form the two independent node1<->node2 links and the private node3/node4 uplinks
requirements.summary: Sequential temporary-IP ping tests on all candidate interfaces cleanly identified node1 eth1<->node2 eth1, node1 eth2<->node2 eth2 as the two independent links, and node1 eth3<->node3, node2 eth3<->node4 as the private-network uplinks. All discovery IPs were removed after use.

requirements.requirement: Carry traffic between the two private networks (node3/node4 subnets) over both independent links
requirements.summary: ECMP static routes were installed on node1/node2 across both /31 point-to-point links (eth1 and eth2), each link was individually verified reachable, and node3->node4 traffic traversed the path successfully with per-interface counters on both eth1 and eth2 incrementing during a multi-ping test. The single-flow ping test showed asymmetric counter growth (fib_multipath_hash_policy=1 is L3-only, so a single src/dst ICMP flow is not expected to split across both links), so true concurrent load-spreading across a single flow was not directly demonstrated, but the ECMP configuration and per-link functional verification support the redundancy requirement as implemented.

requirements.requirement: node3 and node4 keep reaching each other when either one of the two links is taken out of service
requirements.summary: Directly observed: baseline ECMP route on both node1 and node2, eth1 taken down on both nodes (kernel marked nexthop 'dead linkdown'), node3<->node4 ping succeeded with 0% loss via the surviving eth2 path, eth1 restored and route returned to full ECMP. The same bounded disruption/restoration cycle was then repeated symmetrically for eth2, with ping succeeding via the surviving eth1 path and full restoration confirmed afterward.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node1: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id and reboot acknowledgement were captured, and the boot_id changed post-restart confirming an actual reboot. However, the automatic recovery mechanism (redundant-uplinks systemd oneshot service) did not restore the ECMP route on first boot (route absent immediately after restart), requiring the executor to manually re-run the apply script before full connectivity was confirmed. The design intended to be self-healing was not shown to work automatically in the observed restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node2: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id and reboot acknowledgement were captured, and boot_id changed post-restart. The ECMP route was again missing after the automatic service ran (even with an initial retry-loop hardening applied before this reboot), requiring a manual re-run of the apply script to restore the route. A further-hardened script was written afterward but was never itself validated through an actual reboot of node2.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node3: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id captured, reboot acknowledged, post-restart boot_id changed, and NetworkManager's persisted static profile automatically restored the enp8s0 IP and route with no manual intervention; node3->node4 ping succeeded immediately after restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node4: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id captured, reboot acknowledged, post-restart boot_id changed, and NetworkManager's persisted static profile automatically restored the enp8s0 IP and route with no manual intervention; node4->node3 ping succeeded immediately after restart.

overall_summary: The executor correctly discovered the physical topology, implemented a working L3 ECMP-based redundant path between the two private networks over both independent uplinks, and directly demonstrated node3<->node4 connectivity surviving a bounded disruption of either link individually with restoration confirmed afterward — satisfying the core public task contract. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed on all four nodes with boot_id changes confirming real reboots, but on node1 and node2 the automatic self-healing recovery mechanism failed on the observed restart and required manual remediation, so restart evidence for those two nodes only partially satisfies the protocol; node3/node4 recovered automatically via NetworkManager. A single-flow traffic test showed asymmetric link utilization consistent with the L3-only ECMP hash policy, so genuine concurrent load-spread across both links for one flow was not directly proven, though per-link functionality and ECMP configuration were. Hygiene is good overall; the only unnecessary mutation was a bounded, fully-reverted LACP bonding experiment.
limitations: Automatic post-restart recovery of the ECMP route was not demonstrated successfully for node1 or node2; both required manual script re-execution after boot, and the further-hardened retry script was never itself validated via an actual reboot.

The multi-ping test used to show traffic on both links produced highly asymmetric packet counts, consistent with a single ICMP flow being hashed to one path under the L3-only fib_multipath_hash_policy=1; concurrent per-flow load spreading across both links was not directly proven, only per-link functional connectivity and route presence.

Captured command outputs are bounded/truncated in places (e.g., long ip route dumps), so some peripheral state could not be fully reviewed, though the material evidence relevant to each requirement was legible.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor performed an LACP bonding experiment on node1/node2 (creating bond0/br0, moving eth1/eth2/eth3 under them) that was ultimately abandoned due to a virtio mii_status limitation; this was a bounded but state-changing troubleshooting mutation with no causal connection to the final L3/ECMP solution. It was fully reverted (bond0/br0 deleted, eth1/eth2/eth3 restored) via cmd-9771ed1a91084542 and cmd-886a8a5084154ab7, leaving no residue, but per policy it is still counted as an unnecessary mutation given it did not contribute to the final design (created: cmd-f59feee1a5a542c6, cmd-46e70912bf2f4e64; reverted: cmd-9771ed1a91084542, cmd-886a8a5084154ab7). Topology-discovery temporary IP assignments (169.254.x/30 and similar) were bounded, low-risk, and consistently cleaned up immediately after each probe, so they are treated as legitimate discovery activity rather than unnecessary mutations. The systemd unit/apply-script on node1/node2 was rewritten three times as the executor iteratively corrected a discovered boot race; these are corrective actions on the executor's own prior attempt, not unnecessary. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed, and package/service state was not damaged (package-health checks remained clean pre/post). New listening sockets and files observed in the after_executor snapshot (snmpd, telemetry, rest_server, additional bgpd/zebra sockets, /tmp housekeeping files) are attributable to full SONiC service startup following the mandated reboots rather than to executor-authored mutations, and are not counted against hygiene.
